descriptor.title: Plasma voriconazole after oral gavage, infected mice (digitized means and error-bar ends)
descriptor.source_notes:
Plasma voriconazole after oral gavage, infected mice (digitized means and error-bar ends)
S03 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.00606-10 | Fig. 2 (Mavridou et al. 2010)
Female CD-1 mice 20-22 g, 4-5 weeks, NON-neutropenic; disseminated aspergillosis (A. fumigatus AZN 8196 i.v.). Voriconazole oral solution by gavage once daily, 10, 40 or 80 mg/kg, from 24 h after infection. PK blood sampled on DAY 2 OF TREATMENT (methods: "immediately before administration of voriconazole and at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, and 24 h postdosing"; text: "8 time points"), 3 mice per time point, lithium-heparin plasma, HPLC-fluorescence, LLOQ 0.01 mg/liter for low concentrations.
Caption: each symbol is the geometric mean and standard deviation of plasma levels for three mice; methods say arithmetic means were calculated. The plotted times (0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 h; axis ends at 15 h) differ from the sampling times in the methods.
Digitized from a 400-dpi render; linear y axis calibrated on ticks 0-50 mg/L, x on ticks 0-15 h; checked against Table 2 Cmax (1.61, 11.81, 35.86 mg/liter). Reading uncertainty about ±0.2 mg/L.
At 0 h the three markers overlap at about 0-1.5 mg/L and were not digitized. The lines continue past 12 h to the axis edge without a marker. Error-bar ends are given only where the bar extends beyond the marker; empty means hidden inside the marker.
10 mg/kg markers at 8 and 12 h are centred on the x axis (read as 0); Table 2 gives Cmin 0.36 mg/liter for this dose. These are digitized means, not individual mice.

descriptor.title: Pharmacokinetic parameters of voriconazole after doses of 10 to 80 mg/kg by oral gavage
descriptor.source_notes:
Pharmacokinetic parameters of voriconazole after doses of 10 to 80 mg/kg by oral gavage
S03 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.00606-10 | Table 2 (checked against the PDF)
Female CD-1 mice 20-22 g, 4-5 weeks, NON-neutropenic; disseminated aspergillosis (A. fumigatus AZN 8196 i.v.). Voriconazole oral solution by gavage once daily, 10, 40 or 80 mg/kg, from 24 h after infection. PK blood sampled on DAY 2 OF TREATMENT (methods: "immediately before administration of voriconazole and at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, and 24 h postdosing"; text: "8 time points"), 3 mice per time point, lithium-heparin plasma, HPLC-fluorescence, LLOQ 0.01 mg/liter for low concentrations.
No footnotes. The fAUC column unit is printed as "mg·h/liter·kg", the same as the dose-normalized AUC column. Text: "The AUC normalized to a dose of 10 mg/kg resulted in ratios of 0.31, 1.75, and 3.68"; "Clearance decreased with increasing doses, showing nonlinearity."
Unbound fraction by ultrafiltration of pooled 1, 2, 4 h plasma (n = 3 per dosing arm): "26.51%, 33.28%, and 30.59% for the 10-, 40-, and 80-mg/kg groups"; "geometric mean unbound voriconazole fraction for all groups combined (n = 9) was 29.97% (95% confidence interval [95% CI], 27.56 to 32.59%)". Discussion: "29.87% (standard deviation, 2.9%)".

descriptor.title: Survival outcome, disseminated aspergillosis (text values)
descriptor.source_notes:
Survival outcome, disseminated aspergillosis (text values)
S03 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.00606-10 | Results text and abstract
Same mice; infected via the lateral tail vein with the 10% survival dose of each isolate. Oral gavage once daily for 14 days from 24 h after infection: 10 and 40 mg/kg for all four isolates, 80 mg/kg for the TR/L98H isolate only (Fig. 1 caption); placebo groups got "single doses of saline by oral gavage"; n = 11 per group. Remaining mice euthanized on day 15 after infection.
Endpoint survival, not fungal burden. Four A. fumigatus isolates (MICs in In_vitro_MIC). Survival curves and dose-survival plots are figures only (not digitized).
Published analysis results, quoted as printed.

descriptor.title: Serum PK parameters given in the Fig. 1 legend, neutropenic infected mice
descriptor.source_notes:
Serum PK parameters given in the Fig. 1 legend, neutropenic infected mice
S02 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.47.10.3165-3169.2003 | Fig. 1 legend and Results text (Andes et al. 2003)
Female ICR/Swiss mice 23-27 g, neutropenic (cyclophosphamide 150 mg/kg day -4, 100 mg/kg day -1), infected (disseminated candidiasis). Single ORAL GAVAGE 10, 20, 40 mg/kg; retro-orbital SERUM, 3 mice per time, every 1-2 h over 5 h; microbiological agar-well assay (Candida kefyr), detection limit 0.25 µg/ml; at 10 mg/kg only 2 time points were above the limit.
Concentration-time points are in Fig. 1 only (geometric mean ± SD of 3 mice; not digitized). Values below are transcribed from the legend text, not read from the plot.
Results text: "The elimination half-life ranged from 0.72 to 2.9 h." (legend gives 0.68 h at 10 mg/kg). Protein binding: "The level of protein binding in mouse serum was 78% at concentrations of 10 and 100 μg/ml."

descriptor.title: Voriconazole efficacy against 10 C. albicans isolates, disseminated candidiasis model
descriptor.source_notes:
Voriconazole efficacy against 10 C. albicans isolates, disseminated candidiasis model
S02 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.47.10.3165-3169.2003 | Table 1
Neutropenic mice as in the PK block; 0.1 ml inoculum (10^4.8-10^5.9 CFU/ml) via the lateral tail vein 2 h before therapy. Isolate K-1: 24 regimens, six total doses (0.078, 0.3125, 1.25, 5, 20, 80 mg/kg/24 h) each split every 3, 6, 12 or 24 h; other isolates: six total doses 0.08-320 mg/kg/24 h split every 6 h "for the 24-h study period".
Groups of two mice per regimen; drug given in 0.2-ml volumes, route of PD dosing not stated (PK used oral gavage). Kidneys removed "at the end of therapy"; the K-1 section gives no explicit duration. Endpoint change in log10 CFU per pair of kidneys (detection limit 100 CFU/kidneys).
MICs by NCCLS M27-A at 48 h (geometric mean of 3); inhibition endpoint not stated. Fluconazole MIC column is a comparator drug. Per-regimen CFU values are in figures only (not transcribed). Header printed over two rows; "Voriconzole" spelled as printed. No footnotes.

PK parameters after intraperitoneal dosing, non-neutropenic infected mice
S04 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.01491-16 | Table 2 (Rudramurthy et al. 2017)
Female Swiss albino mice 20-25 g, 4-5 weeks, non-neutropenic, disseminated A. flavus infection. INTRAPERITONEAL 5, 10, 20, 40 mg/kg once daily for 7 days from 24 h after infection. Footnote a: "AUC∞_pred, AUC extrapolated to infinity using the last predicted concentration; AUC∞_D_pred, dose-normalized AUC∞_pred." Unbound fraction not measured; the authors used 29.87% from S03. Concentrations in Fig. 2 only (not digitized).

descriptor.title: Survival ED50 by A. flavus isolate (text values)
descriptor.source_notes:
Survival ED50 by A. flavus isolate (text values)
S04 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.01491-16 | Results text
Same model; 0.1 ml conidial suspension via the lateral tail vein at each isolate's LD90, printed as 8 × 10^5 (760690), 1 × 10^6 (761100), 6 × 10^5 (760815) and 8 × 10^5 (761157) with no unit in that sentence. From 24 h after infection, i.p. 5, 10, 20 or 40 mg/kg once daily for 7 consecutive days; controls got "single doses of saline"; n = 11 per group, 220 mice in total. Mice checked at least three times daily and euthanized on day 15.
Endpoint survival. Isolate MICs in In_vitro_MIC. EI50 (AUC/MIC) is shown only in Fig. 5, no number in the text.
Read once from the journal HTML; the first two values were confirmed against short quotes, the last two are single readings.

descriptor.title: Serum voriconazole concentrations in mice given grapefruit juice
descriptor.source_notes:
Serum voriconazole concentrations in mice given grapefruit juice
S05 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.45.2.601-604.2001 | Table 1 (Sugar & Liu 2001)
Male BALB/cByJ mice (weight not reported), intranasal Blastomyces dermatitidis. Drinking water replaced by GRAPEFRUIT JUICE (about "2 to 3 ml of grapefruit juice/day") from 5 days before infection to raise exposure (CYP inhibition).
Oral gavage in 4% PEG 400, 5, 20 or 40 mg/kg daily or 40 mg/kg three times a week, from day 5 after infection for 21 days. Serum agar-well bioassay (C. kefyr), standard curve 0.6125-10 μg/ml.
Footnote a: "Values are means ± standard deviations of values obtained from six mice at each time point. Blood was obtained on day 11 (midtreatment, approximately 4 h after dosing) and day 23, 2 days after treatment was stopped. Day 11 was Thursday, and thus, mice in the group that received voriconazole at 40 mg/kg three times per week (on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays) received voriconazole approximately 24 h earlier."

descriptor.title: Pharmacokinetic parameters after single IV and oral voriconazole, with and without tofacitinib
descriptor.source_notes:
Pharmacokinetic parameters after single IV and oral voriconazole, with and without tofacitinib
S08 | DOI 10.3390/pharmaceutics13050740 | Table 2 (Lee et al. 2021; read from the PDF)
Male Sprague-Dawley rats, about 7 weeks, 230-240 g at purchase (table gives body weight at study). IV 10 mg/kg over 1 min via the jugular vein (4 mL/kg; 0.9% NaCl containing 50% PEG 400); oral 20 mg/kg by gastric gavage (6 mL/kg). Carotid-artery plasma; HPLC with fluorescence detection; LLOQ not stated in the text read.
IV sampling 0, 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 600 and/or 720 min; oral 0-960 min. Urine 0-24 h and whole GI tract at 24 h. Concentration curves are in Fig. 3 only (not digitized). "Values are means ± standard deviation (SD)."
"With TFC" columns are a drug-interaction condition (tofacitinib 10 mg/kg IV or 20 mg/kg oral given together), not voriconazole alone. IV with-TFC n is 6 in the methods and 5 in the table. Footnote: "* Significantly different from respective control group (p < 0.05)."
Text: Vss with tofacitinib "significantly greater (127%)", but the table shows no asterisk on Vss. F is AUC oral / AUC IV per the methods; printed values 106 and 122.

descriptor.title: Population pharmacokinetic parameters of VOR in rats (autoinduction model)
descriptor.source_notes:
Population pharmacokinetic parameters of VOR in rats (autoinduction model)
S06 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.01556-08 | Table 2 (van de Sande et al. 2009)
Neutropenic female RP strain albino rats (age and weight not reported); PK groups of 9 uninfected neutropenic rats. Vfend INTRAPERITONEAL q12h for 10 days in four regimens: 2.6 mg/kg; 5 mg/kg; 6, 8, 10, 11 mg/kg on days 1-4 then 12 mg/kg; 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15 mg/kg on days 1-4 then 17.5 mg/kg. Sampling days 0, 5 and 9, three times per rat (0, 2, 8 h; 0.5, 4, 10 h; 1, 6, 12 h); retro-orbital plasma; agar-diffusion bioassay (C. albicans), standards 0.125-4 µg/ml; binding not measured.
NONMEM model with Michaelis-Menten elimination and enzyme autoinduction: "the amount of enzyme is increased sixfold on the last day, producing a comparable increase in the Vmax." Footnote a: "Standard errors of the estimates were <42%." V in ml and Vmax in μg/h are per animal.
Measured concentrations are in Fig. 1 only (days 0 and 9 at 7.5 and 17.5 mg/kg; not digitized; legend does not say whether dots are individual rats).

Final population PK model, healthy and cryptococcal-meningitis rats
S07 | DOI 10.1128/AAC.00321-17 | Table 1 (Alves et al. 2017)
Male Wistar rats 150-350 g; 12 rats (7 healthy, 5 infected with Cryptococcus neoformans, studied day 10 after infection). Single IV bolus 5 mg/kg (tail vein). Plasma at 0.08, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 h by LC-MS/MS (LLOQ 0.05 μg/ml); brain microdialysate every 30 min by LC-UV (free brain concentration).
Footnote: "NA, not applicable; RSE, relative standard error (standard error of estimate/estimate × 100)." VM printed in μg/ml; kM fixed from a previous study. V1 and V2 are per animal (liters). Covariate, residual-error and AIC rows were not confirmed and are omitted.
Plasma protein binding by ultrafiltration (0.075, 0.4, 0.8 μg/ml): "were found to be 65% ± 2.5% for healthy animals and 64% ± 1.3% for infected animals (P < 0.05)."

descriptor.title: SECONDARY, LOW CONFIDENCE: multi-species PK table adapted from Roffey et al. 2003
descriptor.linked_notes:
SECONDARY, LOW CONFIDENCE: multi-species PK table adapted from Roffey et al. 2003
S01 | No DOI; de Araujo BV 2008 doctoral thesis, UFRGS, lume.ufrgs.br/bitstream/handle/10183/12602/000628550.pdf | Tabela 2.5 / "Tabela 5." p.26; adapted from Roffey SJ et al. Drug Metab Dispos 2003;31:731-741, DOI 10.1124/dmd.31.6.731 (original not accessed)
SECONDARY SOURCE. A thesis reproduction of Roffey 2003 ("Adaptado de ROFFEY et al., 2003"); the original paper was not available, so no value here has been checked against it. Treat every value as low confidence.
Title: "Parâmetros farmacocinéticos do voriconazol em diversas espécies animais." Header as extracted has 5 species names (Camundongo | Rato | Coelho | Cobaio | Cão) but 6 data columns, because rat has male and female columns.
Column mapping by header order is NOT_VERIFIED: col1 mouse, col2 rat male, col3 rat female, col4 rabbit, col5 guinea pig, col6 dog. Two text extractions gave opposite n for col4 and col5 (rabbit n = 1 and guinea pig n = 3, or the reverse). The dog binding of 51% is also quoted in a horse study.
Footnote: "*=Ligação as Proteínas Plasmáticas; u = dose única; m = dose múltipla (uma vez ao dia por 10 dias), exceto para cobaio (3 vezes ao dia)." ASC = AUC; LPP = plasma protein binding (%). Decimal commas are Portuguese (41,7 means 41.7).
"f" has no unit or definition in the table; two values exceed 100. AUC end time t, multiple-dose sampling day, formulation and matrix are not given.
